title.zh: 卷3 帝紀第3 孝閔帝
title.raw: 卷3 帝紀第3 孝閔帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Xiaomin

sentences.zh: 孝閔皇帝諱覺，字陁羅尼，太祖第三子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaomin’s taboo name was Jue, his style Tuoluoni, and he was the Grand Duke’s third son.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaomin Emperor, taboo name Jue and styled Tuoluoni, was the third son of the Grand Duke.

sentences.zh: 母曰元皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was the Empress Yuan.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，生於同州官舍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, he was born in the official residence at Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Datong he was born in the government quarters at Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 九歲，封略陽郡公。

translations.literal: At nine sui he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of nine he was made Duke of Lueyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時有善相者史元華見帝，退謂所親曰：「此公子有至貴之相，但恨其壽不足以稱之耳。

translations.literal: At the time there was a skilled physiognomist, Shi Yuanhua, who saw the emperor and, on withdrawing, said to those close to him: “This young lord has the countenance of supreme nobility, but I regret that his allotted years are not enough to match it.”
translations.idiomatic: A skilled physiognomist named Shi Yuanhua once looked upon the future emperor and told his intimates afterward: “This boy bears the marks of the highest eminence—yet his lifespan will fall short of what his face promises.”

sentences.zh: 」魏恭帝三年三月，命為安定公世子。

translations.literal: ” In the third month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was appointed heir to the Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was named heir to the Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 四月，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was appointed General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he received appointment as General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十月乙亥，太祖崩，丙子，嗣位太師、大冢宰。

translations.literal: On the day yihai of the tenth month the Grand Duke died; on the day bingzi [Jue] succeeded to the posts of Grand Preceptor and Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the tenth month the Grand Duke died; on the following day, bingzi, Jue succeeded him as Grand Preceptor and Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁亥，魏帝詔以岐陽之地封帝為周公。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai of the twelfth month the Wei emperor issued an edict enfeoffing the emperor as Duke of Zhou with the territory of Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the twelfth month the Wei emperor decreed that Jue should be enfeoffed as Duke of Zhou with the lands of Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，禪位於帝。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi [the Wei emperor] abdicated the throne to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Wei emperor abdicated in his favor.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「予聞皇天之命不于常，惟歸於德。

translations.literal: The edict said: “We have heard that Heaven’s mandate is not fixed, but goes to the virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: “We have heard that Heaven’s command is not constant—it rests only with the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 故堯授舜，舜授禹，時其宜也。

translations.literal: Thus Yao gave the throne to Shun, and Shun to Yu, because the time was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yao yielded to Shun, and Shun to Yu, each in season with Heaven’s intent.

sentences.zh: 天厭我魏邦，垂變以告，惟爾罔弗知。

translations.literal: Heaven is weary of our Wei state and sends down change to announce it—yet you alone do not know.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has grown weary of the house of Wei and shows its displeasure in portents—yet you alone seem not to see.

sentences.zh: 予雖不明，敢弗龔天命，格有德哉。

translations.literal: Though We are not enlightened, how dare We fail to respect Heaven’s mandate and seek out the virtuous?
translations.idiomatic: Though We lack wisdom, how dare We refuse Heaven’s command or fail to yield to worth?

sentences.zh: 今踵唐虞舊典，禪位於周，庸佈告遐邇焉。

translations.literal: Now We follow the old model of Tang and Yu and abdicate the throne to Zhou—let this be proclaimed far and near.”
translations.idiomatic: We therefore follow the ancient precedent of Tang and Yu and yield the throne to Zhou—let this be proclaimed throughout the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」使大宗伯趙貴持節奉冊書曰：「咨爾周公，帝王之位弗有常，有德者受命，時乃天道。

translations.literal: ” He sent the Grand Director of Ritual Zhao Gui to bear the staff of authority and present the book of investiture, saying: “O Duke of Zhou, the position of emperor and king is not fixed; he who has virtue receives the mandate—such is Heaven’s way.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Director of Ritual Zhao Gui was sent with the staff of authority and the book of investiture, which declared: “O Duke of Zhou, the throne is not forever fixed; the virtuous receive the mandate—such is Heaven’s way.

sentences.zh: 予式時庸，荒求于唐虞之彝踵。

translations.literal: We at this time broadly seek to follow the constant patterns of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At this time We earnestly seek to follow the models left by Tang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 曰我魏德之終舊矣，我邦小大罔弗知，今其可久怫於天道而不歸有德歟。

translations.literal: We say: the end of Wei virtue is already old; great and small in our state all know it—how can it long resist Heaven’s way and not return to the virtuous?
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of Wei has run its course, and none in the realm doubts it—how can the throne long defy Heaven and refuse the worthy?

sentences.zh: 時用詢謀。

translations.literal: At this time counsel was sought.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel was now sought throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 僉曰公昭考文公，格勳德於天地，丕濟生民。

translations.literal: All said: “Your late father, Duke Wen, achieved meritorious virtue matching Heaven and Earth and greatly aided the people.
translations.idiomatic: All declared: “Your late father Duke Wen matched Heaven and Earth in merit and brought vast benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 洎公躬，又宣重光。

translations.literal: When it reached Your person, you again spread a doubled radiance.
translations.idiomatic: In your own person you have renewed that glory.

sentences.zh: 故玄象徵見於上，謳訟奔走於下，天之歷數，用實在焉。

translations.literal: Therefore celestial signs appeared above and songs of praise rushed below—the calendar of Heaven is truly manifest.”
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s signs have appeared above and songs of praise below—the mandate is manifest for all to see.”

sentences.zh: 予安敢弗若。

translations.literal: How could We dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: How could We dare do otherwise?

sentences.zh: 是以欽祗聖典，遜位於公。

translations.literal: Therefore We reverently received the sacred canon and yielded the throne to you.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore reverently bow to the sacred precedent and yield the throne to you.

sentences.zh: 公其享茲大命，保有萬國，可不慎歟。

translations.literal: You shall receive this great mandate and preserve the myriad states—can you not be cautious?”
translations.idiomatic: Receive this great mandate, preserve the myriad realms, and govern with care.”

sentences.zh: 」魏帝臨朝，遣民部中大夫、濟北西元迪致皇帝璽紱。

translations.literal: ” The Wei emperor attended court and sent Yuan Di of the Western Commandery of Jibei, Gentleman of the Ministry of the People, to present the imperial seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor came to court and sent Yuan Di of Western Jibei, Gentleman of the Ministry of the People, to present the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: [Jue] firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Jue firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 公卿百辟勸進，太

translations.literal: The dukes, ministers, and hundred officials urged him to accept; the Grand
translations.idiomatic: The dukes, ministers, and all officials pressed him to ascend; the Grand

translations.literal: (Preceptor)
translations.idiomatic: (Grand Preceptor)

sentences.zh: 〔史〕陳祥瑞，乃從之。

translations.literal: [Historian] Chen presented auspicious omens, and only then did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: the historian Chen presented auspicious omens, and only then did he accept.

sentences.zh: 是日，魏帝遜于大司馬府。

translations.literal: That day the Wei emperor withdrew to the residence of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Wei emperor retired to the Grand Marshal’s residence.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，祠圓丘。

translations.literal: On the day renyin he sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he offered sacrifice at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「予本自神農，其於二丘，宜作厥主。

translations.literal: An edict said: “We trace our origin to Shen Nong; for the two mounds he should serve as their lord.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: “Our line descends from Shen Nong; at the two mounds he shall be chief among the spirits.

sentences.zh: 始祖獻侯，啟土遼海，肇有國基，配南北郊。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor Duke Xianhou opened the land beyond the Liao Sea and first established the foundation of the state; he is paired at the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Founding Ancestor Duke Xianhou opened the northeast and laid the state’s foundation; he is honored at the southern and northern suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 文考德符五運，受天明命，祖于明堂，以配上帝，廟為太祖。

translations.literal: Cultured Father’s virtue accorded with the five cycles and received Heaven’s bright mandate; at the Bright Hall he is honored as ancestor to match the Supreme Lord, and his temple is titled Grand Ancestor.”
translations.idiomatic: Cultured Father’s virtue embraced the five phases and received Heaven’s mandate; in the Bright Hall he is honored to match the Supreme Lord, and his temple is titled Grand Ancestor.”

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，祠方丘。

translations.literal: On the day guimao he sacrificed at the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he sacrificed at the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，祠太社。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen he sacrificed at the Grand Altar of Soil.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he sacrificed at the Grand Altar of Soil.

sentences.zh: 初除市門稅。

translations.literal: Market-gate taxes were abolished for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time, market-gate taxes were abolished.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，祠太廟。

translations.literal: On the day yisi he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 丁未，會百官於乾安殿，班賞各有差。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei he assembled the hundred officials in the Qian’an Hall and distributed rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he gathered the officials in the Qian’an Hall and bestowed rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「上天有命，革魏於周，致予一人，受茲大號。

translations.literal: On the day wushen an edict said: “Heaven has commanded the change from Wei to Zhou and brought Us alone to receive this great title.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen an edict proclaimed: “Heaven has ordered the transformation from Wei to Zhou and set Us alone to bear this great title.

sentences.zh: 予惟古先聖王，罔弗先于省視風俗，以求民瘼，然後克治。

translations.literal: We reflect that the ancient sage kings never failed first to examine customs and seek the people’s afflictions, and only then could they achieve good rule.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage kings always examined local customs and sought out the people’s hardships before they could govern well—and so must We.

sentences.zh: 矧予眇眇，又當草昧，若弗尚于達四聰、明四目之訓者，其有聞知哉。

translations.literal: How much more when We are so slight, and moreover at the beginning of establishment—if We do not honor the teaching of reaching the four ears and clarifying the four eyes, what will reach Our hearing?
translations.idiomatic: How much more in Our slight person, at the founding of a new dynasty—if We neglect to open Our ears and eyes to all quarters, what will ever reach Us?

sentences.zh: 有司宜分命方別之使，所在巡撫。

translations.literal: The responsible offices should dispatch envoys to the separate regions to tour and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices send envoys to every region to tour and inspect.

sentences.zh: 五教何者不宣，時政有何不便；

translations.literal: Which of the five teachings are not proclaimed, and which current policies are not convenient;
translations.idiomatic: Whether the five teachings have not reached, and what policies cause hardship;

sentences.zh: 得無脩身潔己，才堪佐世之人，而不為上所知；

translations.literal: whether there are none who cultivate themselves and possess talent fit to aid the age yet are unknown to their superiors;
translations.idiomatic: whether men of talent who cultivate themselves remain unknown to the throne;

sentences.zh: 冤枉受罰，幽辱于下之徒，而不為上所理；

translations.literal: whether there are none who suffer unjust punishment and languish in obscurity yet are not redressed by their superiors;
translations.idiomatic: whether the wrongly punished and the disgraced go unredressed;

sentences.zh: 孝義貞節，不為有司所申；

translations.literal: whether filial devotion, righteousness, and chaste integrity are not reported by the responsible offices;
translations.idiomatic: whether filial sons, the righteous, and the chaste fail to receive official commendation;

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤窮，不為有司所恤；

translations.literal: whether widowers, orphans, and the destitute are not comforted by the responsible offices;
translations.idiomatic: whether widowers, orphans, and the destitute lack official relief;

sentences.zh: 暨黎庶衣食豐約，賦役繁省，災厲所興，水旱之處：並宜具聞。

translations.literal: and whether the people’s food and clothing are abundant or scant, taxes and corvée heavy or light, where calamities arise, and where flood or drought occur: all should be fully reported.
translations.idiomatic: and whether the people have food and clothing, whether taxes are heavy or light, where disasters strike, and where flood or drought afflict the land—all must be reported in full.

sentences.zh: 若有年八十已上，所在就加禮餼。

translations.literal: If there are any eighty sui or more, wherever they are found, ceremonial gifts should be added on the spot.”
translations.idiomatic: Wherever anyone has reached eighty years, local officials shall present ceremonial gifts on the spot.”

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，祠南郊。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 壬子，立王后元氏。

translations.literal: On the day renzi he established Lady Yuan as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he installed Lady Yuan as empress.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔曰：「惟天地草昧，建邦以寧。

translations.literal: On the day yimao an edict said: “When Heaven and Earth were in chaos, states were founded to bring tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict said: “When Heaven and Earth were still unordered, states were raised up to bring peace.

sentences.zh: 今可大啟諸國，為周藩屏。

translations.literal: Now the various states may be broadly enfeoffed to serve as Zhou’s screen of defense.”
translations.idiomatic: Let the feudal states now be broadly enfeoffed to serve as Zhou’s protective screen.”

sentences.zh: 」於是封太師李弼為趙國公，太傅趙貴為楚國公，太保獨孤信為衛國公，大司寇于謹為燕國公，大司空侯莫陳崇為梁國公，大司馬、中山公護為晉國公，邑各萬戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Preceptor Li Bi was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, Grand Tutor Zhao Gui as Duke of Chu, Grand Protector Dugu Xin as Duke of Wei, Grand Minister of Justice Yu Jin as Duke of Yan, Grand Minister of Works Houmochen Chong as Duke of Liang, Grand Marshal the Duke of Zhongshan Hu as Duke of Jin—each with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Li Bi became Duke of Zhao; Grand Tutor Zhao Gui, Duke of Chu; Grand Protector Dugu Xin, Duke of Wei; Grand Minister of Justice Yu Jin, Duke of Yan; Grand Minister of Works Houmochen Chong, Duke of Liang; and Grand Marshal the Duke of Zhongshan, Hu, Duke of Jin—each with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，祠太廟。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，親耕籍田。

translations.literal: On the day guihai he personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he performed the spring plowing rite in person.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，於劍南陵井置陵州，武康郡置資州，遂寧郡置遂州。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin Ling Province was established at Jianjing in Nanling on the Sword Road; Zi Province at Wukang commandery; and Sui Province at Suining commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Ling Province was created at Jianjing in Nanling; Zi Province at Wukang; and Sui Province at Suining.

sentences.zh: 二月癸酉，朝日於東郊。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou of the second month he worshipped the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the second month he worshipped the sun at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，改封永昌郡公廣為天水郡公。

translations.literal: On the day yihai the Duke of Yongchang commandery Guang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Duke Guang of Yongchang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，祠太社。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin he sacrificed at the Grand Altar of Soil.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he sacrificed at the Grand Altar of Soil.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，楚國公趙貴謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai Duke of Chu Zhao Gui plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Zhao Gui, Duke of Chu, plotted rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared:

sentences.zh: 朕文考昔與群公洎列將眾官，同心戮力，共治天下。

translations.literal: Our Cultured Father in the past, together with the various dukes and with the ranked generals and the host of officials, with one heart and shared strength jointly governed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Our Cultured Father once joined the great dukes, the generals, and all officials in single-minded effort to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 自始及終，二十三載，迭相匡弼，上下無怨。

translations.literal: From beginning to end, twenty-three years, they aided one another in turn, and above and below harbored no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-three years they supported one another without rancor between high and low.

sentences.zh: 是以群公等用升余於大位。

translations.literal: Therefore the various dukes and others used this to raise Us to the great position.
translations.idiomatic: It was thus that they raised Us to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不德，豈不識此。

translations.literal: Though We lack virtue, how could We not know this?
translations.idiomatic: Though We lack virtue, We are not unmindful of this debt.

sentences.zh: 是以朕於群公，同姓者如弟兄，異姓者如甥舅。

translations.literal: Therefore toward the various dukes, those of the same surname We treat as brothers, those of different surnames as maternal uncles and nephews by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the great dukes We treat those of our clan as brothers and those of other lines as uncles and nephews.

sentences.zh: 冀此一心，平定宇內，各令子孫，享祀百世。

translations.literal: We hoped that with this single heart the realm would be pacified and each man’s descendants would enjoy sacrifice for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: We hoped that in unity the realm would be settled and their descendants would offer sacrifice for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 而朕不明，不能輯睦，致使楚公貴不悅于朕，與万俟幾通、叱奴興、王龍仁、長孫僧衍等陰相假署，圖危社稷。

translations.literal: Yet We are not enlightened and could not harmonize them, causing Duke of Chu Gui to be displeased with Us and, with Moqi Jitong, Chinu Xing, Wang Longren, and Yuchi Sengyan and others, secretly to set up false commissions and plot to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet We failed to keep harmony, and Duke of Chu Gui, displeased with Us, joined Moqi Jitong, Chinu Xing, Wang Longren, Yuchi Sengyan, and others in secret plots against the state.

sentences.zh: 事不克行，為開府宇文盛等所告。

translations.literal: The affair could not be carried out and was reported by the Founding Grand Commander Yuwen Sheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed and was denounced by Founding Grand Commander Yuwen Sheng and others.

sentences.zh: 及其推究，咸伏厥辜。

translations.literal: When it was pursued to the end, all confessed their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was investigated to the end, all were found guilty.

sentences.zh: 興言及此，心焉如痗。

translations.literal: To speak of this pains Our heart as though it were pierced.
translations.idiomatic: At the mention of it Our heart is wrung with grief.

sentences.zh: 但法者天下之法，朕旣為天下守法，安敢以私情廢之。

translations.literal: But law is the law of the realm; since We hold the law for the realm, how dare We abolish it for private feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Yet law is the law of all under Heaven; as sovereign We cannot set it aside for private grief.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰「善善及後世，惡惡止其身」，其貴、通、興、龍仁罪止一家，僧衍止一房，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: The Documents says, “Reward the good even to their posterity; stop the evil with the evildoer himself.” Gui, Jitong, Xing, and Longren’s guilt stops with their households; Sengyan’s with his branch alone; all others are not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: As the Documents says: “Extend reward to the descendants of the good; let punishment for evil stop with the evildoer.” Gui, Jitong, Xing, and Longren’s guilt ends with their households; Sengyan’s with his branch; the rest shall not be implicated.

sentences.zh: 惟爾文武，咸知時事。

translations.literal: You civil and military officials all know the timely meaning of this.
translations.idiomatic: Let all you civil and military officials understand the times.

sentences.zh: 太保獨孤信有罪免。

translations.literal: Grand Protector Dugu Xin was found guilty and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Protector Dugu Xin was found guilty and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以大司空、梁國公侯莫陳崇為太保，大司馬、晉國公護為大冢宰，柱國、博陵公賀蘭祥為大司馬，高陽公達奚武為大司寇，大將軍、化政公宇文貴為柱國。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu Grand Minister of Works the Duke of Liang Houmochen Chong was made Grand Protector, Grand Marshal the Duke of Jin Hu was made Grand Chancellor, Grand Duke Helan Xiang of Boling was made Grand Marshal, the Duke of Gaoyang Daxi Wu was made Grand Minister of Justice, and Grand General the Duke of Huazheng Yuwen Gui was made Grand Duke General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Houmochen Chong, Duke of Liang and Grand Minister of Works, became Grand Protector; Hu, Duke of Jin and Grand Marshal, Grand Chancellor; Helan Xiang of Boling, Grand Marshal; Daxi Wu of Gaoyang, Grand Minister of Justice; and Yuwen Gui of Huazheng, Grand Duke General of the Army.

sentences.zh: 己亥，秦州、涇州各獻木連理。

translations.literal: On the day jihai Qin and Jing provinces each presented trees with conjoined branches.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Qin and Jing provinces each presented trees whose branches had grown together.

sentences.zh: 歲星守少微，經六十日。

translations.literal: The Year Star dwelt in Shaowei for sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter remained in Shaowei for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，會文武百官，班賜各有差。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the third month he assembled the civil and military officials and distributed rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the third month he gathered civil and military officials and distributed rewards by rank.

sentences.zh: 己酉，柱國、衛國公獨孤信賜死。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou Grand Duke Dugu Xin of Wei was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Dugu Xin, Grand Duke of Wei, was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔曰：「

translations.literal: On the day renzi an edict said: “
translations.idiomatic: On renzi an edict said: “

translations.literal: (Zhe)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhe Province)

sentences.zh: 〔淅〕州去歲不登，厥民饑饉，朕用慜焉。

translations.literal: [Xi] Province last year did not ripen; its people suffer hunger—We are moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Province failed to ripen last year and its people hunger—We are deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 其當州租輸未畢者，悉宜免之。

translations.literal: All rent and tax deliveries for that province not yet completed should be entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: All unpaid rent and tax still due from that province shall be remitted in full.

sentences.zh: 兼遣使巡檢，有窮餒者，並加賑給。

translations.literal: Envoys are also to be sent to tour and inspect; wherever there are those in desperate want, relief shall be added.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys shall tour the region and give additional relief wherever people face starvation.

sentences.zh: 」癸亥，省六府士員，三分減一。

translations.literal: ” On the day guihai the gentlemen attached to the six ministries were reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the staff of the six ministries was cut by one-third.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己巳，以少師、平原公侯莫陳順為柱國。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jisi, the Junior Preceptor the Duke of Pingyuan Houmochen Shun was made Grand Duke General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the fourth month of summer Houmochen Shun, Junior Preceptor and Duke of Pingyuan, was made Grand Duke General of the Army.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔死罪以下，各降一等。

translations.literal: On the day renshen an edict ordered that all below the death penalty be reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen an edict reduced by one degree all sentences below death.

sentences.zh: 壬午，謁成陵。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he visited Chengling.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he visited Chengling.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，祠太廟。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 五月癸卯，歲星犯太微上將，太白犯軒轅。

translations.literal: On the day guimao of the fifth month the Year Star encroached on the Senior General in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and the White Planet encroached on Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the fifth month Jupiter trespassed on the Senior General in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and Venus on Xuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 己酉，槐里獻白燕。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou Huaili presented a white swallow.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Huaili presented a white swallow.

sentences.zh: 帝欲觀漁於昆明池，博士姜須諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to watch fishing at Kunming Pool; Academician Jiang Xu remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to watch fishing at Kunming Pool; Academician Jiang Xu remonstrated, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬寅，帝聽訟於右寢，多所哀宥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day renyin, the emperor heard lawsuits in the right sleeping chamber and showed much leniency.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the seventh month of autumn he heard cases in the right sleeping chamber and showed much mercy.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，月掩心後星。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen the moon eclipsed the star behind the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the moon occulted the star behind the Heart.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，祠太廟。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯東井北端第二星。

translations.literal: The Sparkling Deluder encroached on the second star at the northern end of the Well.
translations.idiomatic: Mars trespassed on the second star at the northern end of the Well constellation.

sentences.zh: 八月戊辰，祠太社。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuchen, he sacrificed at the Grand Altar of Soil.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the eighth month he sacrificed at the Grand Altar of Soil.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔曰：「朕甫臨大位，政教未孚，使我民農，多陷刑網。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei an edict said: “We have just ascended the great throne; government and teaching are not yet trusted, causing Our farming people to fall often into the penal net.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei an edict declared: “Having just taken the throne, We have not yet won the people’s trust in Our rule, and many farmers have been caught in the courts.

sentences.zh: 今秋律已應，將行大戮，言念羣生，責在於朕。

translations.literal: Now the autumn pitch has sounded and great executions are about to be carried out; when We think of the multitude, the blame lies with Us.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn has come and executions are at hand; when We think of the people, the fault is Ours alone.

sentences.zh: 宜從肆眚，與其更新。

translations.literal: We should follow the broad pardon and grant them renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Let a great amnesty be proclaimed and give them a new start.

sentences.zh: 其犯〔死〕者宜降從流，流以下各降一等。

translations.literal: Those guilty of [death] should be reduced to exile; below exile, each degree should be reduced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Death sentences shall be commuted to exile, and all lesser punishments reduced one degree.

sentences.zh: 不在赦限者，不從此降。

translations.literal: Those outside the scope of the amnesty are not reduced under this measure.
translations.idiomatic: Those excluded from the amnesty shall not benefit from this reduction.

sentences.zh: 」甲午，詔曰：「帝王之治天下，罔弗博求眾才，以乂厥民。

translations.literal: ” On the day jiawu an edict said: “In governing the realm, emperors and kings never fail broadly to seek the many talented to bring peace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu an edict said: “Every ruler who governs the realm must seek talent far and wide to bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 今二十四軍宜舉賢良堪治民者，軍列九人。

translations.literal: Now the twenty-four armies should each recommend worthy men capable of governing the people, nine men per army.
translations.idiomatic: Let each of the twenty-four armies nominate nine worthy men fit to govern the people.

sentences.zh: 被舉之人，於後不稱厥任者，所舉官司，皆治其罪。」

translations.literal: If those recommended later do not fulfill their duties, the recommending office in every case shall be punished for the crime.”
translations.idiomatic: If any nominee later proves unfit for office, the officials who recommended him shall be punished.”

sentences.zh: 九月庚申，詔曰：「朕聞君臨天下者，非由一人，時乃上下同心所致。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day gengshen, an edict said: “We have heard that he who rules the realm as sovereign does not do so alone—it is achieved when high and low are of one heart.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the ninth month an edict said: “A sovereign does not rule alone; the realm is governed when ruler and subjects share one heart.

sentences.zh: 今文武之官及諸軍人不霑爵封者，宜各授兩大階。

translations.literal: Now civil and military officials and all soldiers who have not received enfeoffment or rank should each be granted two great steps.
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials and soldiers who have not yet received titles or fiefs shall each be advanced two full ranks.

sentences.zh: 」改太守為郡守。

translations.literal: ” The title Grand Administrator was changed to Commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The title Grand Administrator was renamed Commandery Administrator.

sentences.zh: 帝性剛果，見晉公護執政，深忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature firm and resolute; seeing Duke of Jin Hu hold power, he deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was firm and decisive by nature, and he deeply resented Duke of Jin Hu’s hold on power.

sentences.zh: 司會李植、軍司馬孫恒以先朝佐命，入侍左右，亦疾護之專，乃與宮伯乙弗鳳、賀拔提等潛謀，請帝誅護。

translations.literal: Director of Accounts Li Zhi and Army Marshal Sun Heng, having aided the founding of the previous reign and attending at his side, also hated Hu’s monopoly of power; they therefore joined Palace Attendants Yifu Feng, Heba Ti, and others in a secret plot and asked the emperor to execute Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, Director of Accounts, and Sun Heng, Army Marshal—both veterans of the founding reign who attended the emperor—likewise hated Hu’s dominance. With Palace Attendants Yifu Feng, Heba Ti, and others they plotted in secret to have the emperor kill him.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave his assent.

sentences.zh: 又引宮伯張光洛同謀。

translations.literal: He also drew in Palace Attendant Zhang Guangluo to the plot.
translations.idiomatic: He also enlisted Palace Attendant Zhang Guangluo in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 光洛密白護，護乃出植為梁州刺史，恆為潼州刺史。

translations.literal: Guangluo secretly informed Hu, and Hu thereupon sent Zhi out as Governor of Liang Province and Heng as Governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Guangluo secretly warned Hu, who promptly sent Zhi to Liang Province and Heng to Tong Province as governors.

sentences.zh: 鳳等遂不自安，更奏帝，將召羣公入，因此誅護。

translations.literal: Feng and the others then could not rest easy and again memorialized the emperor, proposing to summon the various dukes to enter court and thereby execute Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Feng and his allies urged the emperor to summon the great dukes to court and kill Hu in the act.

sentences.zh: 光洛又白之。

translations.literal: Guangluo again informed Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangluo again betrayed the plot to Hu.

sentences.zh: 時小司馬尉遲綱總統宿衛兵，護乃召綱共謀廢立。

translations.literal: At the time Junior Army Marshal Yuchi Gang commanded the palace guard; Hu therefore summoned Gang to join him in plotting deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Army Marshal Yuchi Gang then commanded the palace guard; Hu summoned him to plan the emperor’s removal.

sentences.zh: 令綱入殿中，詐呼鳳等論事。

translations.literal: He ordered Gang to enter the palace hall and falsely summon Feng and the others to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had Gang enter the hall and call Feng and the others under pretense of business.

sentences.zh: 旣至，以次執送護第，並誅之。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they were seized in order and sent to Hu’s residence, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: As each arrived he was seized and taken to Hu’s house, and all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 綱仍罷散禁兵，帝方悟，無左右，獨在內殿，令宮人持兵自守。

translations.literal: Gang then dismissed and dispersed the palace guard; the emperor only then realized what had happened. With no attendants, he was alone in the inner hall and ordered palace women to take up arms in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Gang then disbanded the palace guard. Only then did the emperor understand; left alone in the inner hall, he had the palace women arm themselves for his defense.

sentences.zh: 護又遣大司馬賀蘭祥逼帝遜位。

translations.literal: Hu also sent Grand Marshal Helan Xiang to force the emperor to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: Hu then sent Grand Marshal Helan Xiang to compel his abdication.

sentences.zh: 遂幽於舊邸，月餘日，以弒崩，時年十六。

translations.literal: He was thereupon confined in his old residence; after more than a month he died by assassination, aged sixteen sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned in his former residence and, a little over a month later, was assassinated at the age of sixteen.

sentences.zh: 植、恆等亦遇害。

translations.literal: Zhi, Heng, and the others also met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Heng, and their fellows were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 及武帝誅護後，乃詔曰：「慎始敬終，有國彝典；

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu executed Hu, an edict said: “To be careful at the beginning and respectful at the end is the constant canon of a state;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu killed Hu, he issued an edict: “Care at the beginning and reverence at the end are the enduring laws of statecraft;

sentences.zh: 事亡如存，哲王通制。

translations.literal: to treat the departed as if they still lived is the universal rule of sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: to honor the dead as though they still lived is the way of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 義崇追遠，禮貴尊親。

translations.literal: Righteousness exalts honoring the distant past; ritual values revering one’s kin.
translations.idiomatic: Duty bids us honor those who went before; ritual demands that we revere our kin.

sentences.zh: 故略陽公至德純粹，天姿秀傑。

translations.literal: Therefore Duke of Lueyang’s supreme virtue was pure and unmixed, his heavenly endowment outstanding and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lueyang possessed supreme virtue, pure and unalloyed, and a heaven-given brilliance.

sentences.zh: 屬魏祚告終，寶命將改，謳歌允集，歷數攸歸，上協蒼靈之慶，下昭后祇之錫。

translations.literal: When Wei’s fortune reached its end and the precious mandate was about to change, songs of praise gathered truly, and the calendar of rule was his; above he accorded with the blessing of the azure spirit, below he manifested the gift of the earthly lord.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Wei ended and the mandate was about to pass, the people’s acclaim gathered and the throne was rightfully his—blessed by Heaven above and sanctioned by Earth below.

sentences.zh: 而禍生肘腋，釁起蕭牆，白獸噬驂，蒼鷹集殿，幽辱神器，弒酷乘輿，冤結生民，毒流㝢縣。

translations.literal: Yet calamity arose at the elbow and trouble sprang within the palace walls; a white beast devoured the paired horses, a dark hawk gathered on the hall; the sacred vessel was shamed, the imperial carriage cruelly murdered, grievance bound the living people, and poison spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet disaster struck at his very side and treason rose within the palace—a white beast savaged the team, a dark hawk alighted on the hall; the sacred regalia was defiled, the sovereign brutally slain, the people left in bitter wrong, and poison spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 今河海澄清，氛沴消蕩，追尊之禮，宜崇徽號。

translations.literal: Now the rivers and seas are clear, malignant vapors dispersed; the rites of posthumous honor should be raised with a lofty title.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is pacified and evil dispelled, his posthumous honors should be raised to a lofty title.

sentences.zh: 」遣太師、蜀國公

translations.literal: ” He sent Grand Preceptor the Duke of Shu
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Grand Preceptor the Duke of Shu

translations.literal: (Guo)
translations.idiomatic: (Guo [Jiong])

sentences.zh: 〔迥〕於南郊上諡曰孝閔皇帝，陵曰靜陵。

translations.literal: [Jiong] to present at the southern suburb the posthumous title Emperor Xiaomin; his tomb is called Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong to offer at the southern suburb the posthumous title Emperor Xiaomin; his mausoleum is named Jingling.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孝閔承旣安之業，應樂推之運，柴天竺物，正位君臨，邇無異言，遠無異望。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiaomin inherited an already settled enterprise and answered a fortune of willing acclaim; he offered up Heaven’s goods and took the correct position as sovereign—near at hand there was no dissenting speech, far off no contrary hope.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Xiaomin inherited a settled realm and answered the people’s willing acclaim. He offered up the goods of the land and took the throne without dissent near or far.

sentences.zh: 雖黃初代德，太始受終，不之尚也。

translations.literal: Though the Huangchu era received the mandate and the Taishi era received the end, he was not inferior to them.
translations.idiomatic: Even the founding reigns of Wei and Jin were not to be preferred over his accession.

sentences.zh: 然政由寧氏，主懷芒刺之疑；

translations.literal: Yet government proceeded from the Ning clan, and the sovereign harbored the suspicion of a thorn in the flesh;
translations.idiomatic: Yet power lay with the Ning house, and the emperor lived with a thorn in his side;

sentences.zh: 祭則寡人，臣無復子之請。

translations.literal: at sacrifice he stood alone, and his ministers no longer made the petition of a son.
translations.idiomatic: at the sacrifices he stood alone, and his ministers no longer played the part of loyal sons.

sentences.zh: 以之速禍，宜哉。

translations.literal: That he met swift calamity was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder that disaster came upon him so quickly.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The entire chapter has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
